Subject: Conditional retention carveout & SIG/CAIQ evidence

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — AeroMed is moving quickly on a pilot and we have one technical ask from our InfoSec and Clinical Ops teams. For a subset of patient-facing flows (PID=aurora-clinical), we need to retain application debug + request traces for 90 days (our default is 90 for forensic purposes). I understand Redwood’s default tenant log retention is 30 days.

Can Redwood support a customer-specific carveout for 90 days for this tenant only? If so, could you confirm the following items we need for our compliance review: 
- SIG/CAIQ mapping that shows how retention controls are implemented and where exceptions are allowed
- A SOC 2 attestation snippet that references log retention windows (we don’t need raw logs)
- Description of the deletion (proof-of-delete) process once retention period elapses
- Any impact on SLAs or cost for a 90-day carveout

I attached an example spreadsheet with the fields AeroMed has to submit to our procurement/compliance team (AeroMed_SIG_request.xlsx). Please let us know what evidence you can provide and an estimate of time to deliver.

Appreciate the quick turn here — we’re targeting an approval window in the week of May 3.

Thanks,
Alejandra Ruiz
Security & Compliance Lead, AeroMed
alejandra.ruiz@aeromed.com

Attachment: AeroMed_SIG_request.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Hi Alejandra — great to meet you yesterday.

Short answer: we can support customer-specific retention windows, but the path depends on deployment mode and desired guarantees. High-level:
- Hosted (standard): Per-tenant retention changes require Product + Security approval and may have limitations on granularity.
- Dedicated / Private: More flexible; we can configure tenant TTLs to 90d and provide documented evidence.

Next steps I propose: I’ll start an internal approval packet with Security and Compliance that maps to the fields in your spreadsheet. To get moving I’ve attached our internal retention-exception template (retention-exception-template.docx) — please confirm the tenant IDs and whether you want debug traces + request/response payloads retained or only structured telemetry.

Note on evidence: we can provide a SOC 2 excerpt and a mapped CAIQ/controls mapping that shows where retention windows are documented. We cannot provide raw logs in an evidence pack; instead we provide process and attestation artifacts and redaction/retention policies.

Do you want me to loop our Security and Compliance owners directly now? If yes, I’ll copy them on the next email and include a proposed mutual action plan.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com

Thanks for the tag, Maya. Quick answers below: 

1) Artifacts we can provide: SOC 2 attestation excerpt (PDF) that references control families for logging/monitoring (we cannot include raw logs), a CAIQ/controls CSV mapping that highlights retention controls and where tenant-level exceptions are permitted, and a process document describing our scheduled deletion + proof-of-delete hooks. I’ll prepare SOC2_retention_excerpt.pdf and CAIQ_retention_mapping.csv.

2) Approvals: Security + Legal sign-off required for hosted-customer carveouts. For Dedicated/Private deployments Legal generally signs an amendment; Security will validate any compensating controls for extended retention. Estimated lead time after we have a signed MOU/Amendment: 5–8 business days to assemble the evidence pack and produce the DocuSign amendment. If AeroMed is on Dedicated/Private, lead time can be 3–5 days.

3) Platform impact: For hosted customers we may need to apply tenant-scoped retention at the storage layer; this can increase storage costs and impact snapshot/backfill windows. We will include a cost delta estimate in the mutual action plan. No change to runtime latency expected.

Action items I need from Maya / AeroMed:
- Confirm tenant ID(s) and whether payloads (PII) should be retained or redacted.
- Confirm preferred deployment mode (hosted vs. dedicated).
- Sign MOU/amendment so Legal can start.

I’ll assemble the artifacts and share a folder link when ready.

Kimberly Park
